acceptance_criteria.criterion: The `matchRoute()` function does not exist in `server.ts`.
`handleRequest()` dispatches all API traffic via a single call to `dispatchRoute()` — no secondary dispatch path remains.
The route table contains a comment block stating that Section B (keyword-specific) must precede Section C (catch-all) for correctness — not cosmetics.
Every parameterised route in the table uses a RegExp with named capture groups (no positional groups).
All existing GUI server tests (`server-*.test.ts`, `route-structured-format.test.ts`) pass without modification beyond import renames if needed.
All deprecated routes remain functional — requests to deprecated endpoints return the same responses as before the migration.
Routes that previously parsed query parameters via `parseQueryString()` in `matchRoute()` now receive their parameters via the dispatcher's `query` argument and produce identical results.

summary: Migrated all 50+ routes from the ~1,100-line matchRoute() if-else chain into declarative Route entries in buildRoutes(). Deleted matchRoute() entirely. Simplified handleRequest() to a single dispatchRoute() call with 404 fallthrough. Routes organized into Section A (body-parsing, existing), Section B (keyword-specific body-free, both active namespaced and deprecated non-namespaced), Section C (catch-all body-free). JSDoc comment block documents Section B/C ordering constraint as load-bearing. All parameterised routes use RegExp with named capture groups. Query parameters for previously matchRoute-parsed routes (projects list, knowledge list, repos, dialogues, chunks, runs) now received via dispatcher query argument. All 118 test files (3595 tests) pass with no modification.

comments.note: gui/server.ts: The RouteHandler type alias (type RouteHandler = () => Promise<unknown>) was removed as part of this WP since it was only used by matchRoute(). No external consumers were found.

gui/docs/agents/project-manifest/api-surface.md, data-flows.md, constraints.md: These agent-context doc files still reference matchRoute() in their descriptions (e.g. 'GET routes are handled by matchRoute()'). These are out of scope for this WP but should be updated in the Documentation phase to reflect the unified dispatchRoute() pattern.

gui/server.ts buildRoutes(): The routes object array is now approximately 450 lines. A future improvement would be to split the route table into logical sub-builders (e.g. buildProjectRoutes, buildKnowledgeRoutes) and compose them in buildRoutes(). This would improve readability without changing behaviour. Not implemented as it is out of scope for this WP.

gui/server.ts dispatchRoute(): The dispatchRoute() function rebuilds the full route table on every request via buildRoutes(). For high-frequency endpoints, caching the compiled route table (e.g. memoizing by ledgerRoot+configPath) would avoid repeated array allocations. Low impact at current traffic levels.

summary: Verified all 7 acceptance criteria via code inspection, static analysis, and test execution. AC1: matchRoute() absent from server.ts (grep confirmed zero matches). AC2: handleRequest() has exactly one dispatchRoute() call — single dispatch path, no secondary routing. AC3: JSDoc comment block on buildRoutes() explicitly states Section B MUST precede Section C as load-bearing (not cosmetic), with concrete explanation of the shadowing risk. AC4: Static analysis confirmed 52 parameterised regex path entries with 83 named capture groups and 0 positional capture groups. AC5: All targeted tests pass — 77 tests across gui-server.test.ts, route-structured-format.test.ts, server-body-limit.test.ts, server-error-mapping.test.ts, server-info.test.ts, server-knowledge-routes.test.ts, server-queue.test.ts, security-headers.test.ts. Full GUI regression also passes: 55 test files, 1624 tests. AC6: Section B/C ordering verified — deprecated /:slug/keyword routes match correctly before Section C catch-alls. /api/projects/my-project/plan, /synthesis, /health, /work-packages, /work-packages/overview, /work-packages/:wpId, /dialogues, /runs all resolve via Section B routes. AC7: parseQueryString() integration confirmed — all query-parameter routes (GET /api/projects, /api/knowledge, /api/repos, /:repo/:slug/dialogues, /:repo/:slug/chunks, /:repo/:slug/runs/:filename?after=N) forward query args correctly. Percent-encoded values decode transparently. Bare ? returns empty URLSearchParams safely.

comments.note: Edge case: GET /api/projects/:repo/:slug/runs/:filename?after=-1 passes -1 as a valid integer to the handler. The server-side code does not reject negative `after` values — this is acceptable as handler-level validation responsibility, not a routing defect.

The deprecated GET /:slug/runs route resolves via resolveProjectDir() and falls back to the legacy flat path. This is correct, but its test coverage is through integration paths rather than a dedicated test. No regression observed, but a targeted unit test would harden this.

comments.note: server.ts line 850-852 (namespaced GET /:repo/:slug/runs/:filename): Refactored the double-parseInt afterParam pattern. Original: `!isNaN(parseInt(afterParam, 10)) ? parseInt(afterParam, 10) : undefined` — parsed the string twice. Replaced with a single parse: `const afterParsed = afterParam != null ? parseInt(afterParam, 10) : NaN; const afterLine = !isNaN(afterParsed) ? afterParsed : undefined;`. Behavior is identical — the fix is purely cosmetic (eliminates the redundant call). No impact on QA validation.

server.ts line 1009-1011 (deprecated GET /:slug/runs/:filename): Same double-parseInt fix applied to the parallel deprecated route. Both runs/:filename routes now share the same single-parse idiom, making the pattern consistent across the file.

server.ts: The inline SAFE_SLUG_REGEX guard in the two runs routes (GET /:repo/:slug/runs and GET /:repo/:slug/runs/:filename) is intentionally asymmetric with the assertSafeSlug() pattern used in other namespaced routes. This is architecturally correct — assertSafeSlug() is functionally equivalent and the inline approach makes the defense-in-depth explicit for routes that skip resolveRepoName(). No action needed; the comments in the source explain the rationale.

server.ts buildRoutes() + dispatchRoute(): The route table is rebuilt on every request. The developer noted this in the implementation pipeline as a future optimization (memoization by ledgerRoot+configPath). This is acceptable at current traffic levels and should remain as a documented future improvement — not a blocking concern for this WP.
